entry.title: UPDATE: Calendar users in Chile's Aysén region need to update the time zone for all events taking place after 2025-04-05 which are impacted by the new DST rules. On 2025-03-20, Chile's Aysén region adopted a new time zone (IANA: "America/Coyhaique”). This time zone will diverge from the continental Chile time zone “Chile Time” (IANA: “America/Santiago”) after 2025-04-05, by staying at UTC-03. Users in, or operating in, the Aysén region will be impacted: their events taking place after 2025-04-05 will be, by default, in the Chile time zone and will diverge by one hour compared to the new Aysén region local time. Impacted users are recommended to take 2 actions as soon as possible: * Go to Calendar Settings > General > Time zone and set their Primary time zone to “Punta Arenas time” (IANA: "America/Punta_Arenas”). * Update all their events taking place after 2025-04-05 in this region to the “Punta Arenas time”. Additionally, we are working on introducing a new time zone for the Aysén region. We will post a communication update when it will be available in Calendar. We will provide an update by Friday, 2025-04-04 13:00 US/Pacific with current details. If impacted users don’t take action, after 2025-04-05 their calendar will: * Show the wrong time with the “Now” red line on Calendar Web; * Display all events shifted by one hour; * Create new events in the wrong time zone.

entry.title: TS-2025-001
entry.summary: Description: Potential for continued admin console access past inactivity timeout What happened? The admin console session timeout works by recording tailnet-specific activity timestamps on login and from browser requests triggered by user activity. Previously the admin console also erroneously considered the act of switching between multiple tailnets to be a login and recorded a fresh timestamp for the user in the destination tailnet while switching. For tailnets whose users were also members of other tailnets with less strict inactivity timeouts, these users may have been able to continue their access to the admin console for longer than expected if they switched between tailnets and did not time out of the less restrictive tailnet. The issue was present since inactivity timeout was initially released in August 2024, and was fixed in production on March 7th, 2025. A user who switches to a tailnet in which their session has already expired will be logged out and redirected to the login page. Who was affected? Tailnets with admin console session timeout configurations and users who are members of other tailnets with less strict session timeout configurations. What was the impact? Users of tailnets with strict admin console session timeouts may have been able to continue their access to the admin console past expected timeouts by switching to and from other tailnets in the admin console whose console configurations were less strict. What do I need to do? No action is required.

entry.title: Booking.com - Introducing clearer fee & tax breakdown for your reservations
entry.summary:
New!
We’re excited to announce our integration with a new Booking.com’s API, bringing you clearer insights into each reservation’s fees and taxes. Those new informations are available for all Property Managers using Payment by booking (with VCC and Bank transfer), whether you’re using partial or full sync with Booking.com. What’s New? Detailed price breakdown: You’ll now see clearer information on rental fees, cleaning fees, service charges, and city taxes directly in the reservation details as below;
Withheld tax details: In regions where Booking.com withholds tax on your behalf, you’ll see exactly how much was withheld and paid to authorities.
Current balance & VCC info: More visibility on the Virtual Credit Card (VCC) balance, plus its activation and expiration dates.
How Does this affect you? Depending on how Booking.com handles the city tax for each reservation, you’ll see one of these scenarios: 1- Booking.com collects and remits city tax directly to the authorities: Your payment bar will show two payments (one for the rental and one for the withheld tax).
Since Booking.com pays the tax on your behalf, the payment bar will appear “complete.” 2- Booking.com collects the city tax from the guest and includes it in the VCC; you are responsible for remitting the tax: The city tax is included in your total payout, so the payment bar will also appear “complete.”
Don’t forget to pay the tax to your local authorities.
3- Booking.com does not collect the city tax; you must collect and remit it yourself: The payment bar will show the rental amount only (city tax is missing).
You must collect the city tax from guests at check-in and pay it to the authorities.
The city tax is missing from the payment bar, you should collect it before/on check-in.
-> Automatic payment link should be disabled in these cases, Booking.com does not include it in the payment because of regulations. If you have any questions, please reach out to us 🙂 Your Smily team!
